quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What is the purpose of highway markings?

options.text: They are only found in construction zones.
They are usually red and blue in color.

questions.explanation: Highway markings help drivers. They show drivers where to position their vehicles, tell drivers where it is safe to pass, and warn drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: An aggressive driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If an aggressive driver is behind you, get out of their way. Avoid looking at them. Speeding up will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Before moving your vehicle, also adjust your seat, fasten your seat belt, and secure loose items. Do not adjust mirrors while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow. High beams reflect off moisture and make it harder to see.

questions.question: You must make an emergency stop on an interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out and flag down the next vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must stop on the shoulder, turn on your emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if you can. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of fast-moving traffic.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection. Pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and drive in front of the pedestrians.
Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrians cross safely.
questions.explanation: Always yield to pedestrians in an intersection, even if you have a green light. Your safety responsibility includes protecting pedestrians in all situations.

questions.question: A blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog is near you. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop. This protects them from injury.

questions.question: A truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly before the truck or bus turns.
Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the truck or bus finishes turning before you turn.
questions.explanation: Do not try to fit your vehicle between a turning truck or bus and the curb. This can cause a serious crash. Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn.

questions.question: A police officer stops you. What should you do?

options.text: Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.
Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.
Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
Get out and walk toward the patrol car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your vehicle with your hands on the steering wheel and wait for the officer.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands on the steering wheel and tell passengers to keep their hands visible. Stay in your vehicle unless the officer asks you to get out. Wait for the officer to ask for your license, registration, and insurance card.

questions.question: When should you look over your shoulder to check your blind spot?

options.text: When pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your vehicle. Check before turning, changing lanes, or pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending or the road is narrowing ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that the right lane is ending or the road will narrow.

questions.question: You should only drive at the maximum posted speed limit when:
questions.explanation: The posted speed limit is the fastest you can legally drive when conditions are perfect. Drive at the same speed as other traffic, up to the speed limit. All drivers are responsible for driving at a safe speed.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, what should you do?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crossings when they follow traffic signals. When there is no traffic signal, you must stop for pedestrians in a crosswalk, whether it is marked or unmarked.

questions.question: Where is passing prohibited?
questions.explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to pass another vehicle on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings.

questions.question: When should drivers yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to you first.
Only if the pedestrians are not using their phones.

questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle completely at a crosswalk to yield to any pedestrian or vehicle already in the intersection. You may proceed carefully only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: Seat belts work best when worn by:

options.text: Everyone in the car every time you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the car every time you drive.
questions.explanation: Every person in your vehicle should wear a seat belt. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a flying object that can hurt others in the car.

questions.question: When a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the flagger tells you.
Follow what other cars are doing, even if the flagger says otherwise.
Assume the flagger should not be there.
Follow normal traffic laws as if construction is not happening.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the flagger tells you.
questions.explanation: Slow down and follow all directions from signs, flaggers, and police officers in construction zones. Not following their directions is illegal and dangerous to workers.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrians are walking along the road.
Watch for construction workers on the road.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that pedestrians may cross the road ahead. Drivers should be careful and watch for pedestrians.

questions.question: When you see a disabled pedestrian using a guide dog, white cane, or other assistive device, you should yield the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: A pedestrian with a disability using a guide dog, white cane, wheelchair, or other assistive device has the right-of-way on sidewalks and roadways, just like any other pedestrian.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop whenever you see pedestrians. Be extra careful where children are present. Always yield to pedestrians crossing in a crosswalk.

questions.question: What is a sign that someone is driving drunk?

options.text: They drive slower than other traffic.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, jerky movements, and sudden stops.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Three-sided signs tell drivers to slow down at an intersection and be ready to stop for other drivers or pedestrians. You may go when it is safe.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows the nervous system. It reduces alertness and concentration, increases reaction time, and greatly reduces coordination.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the lane is clear.

questions.explanation: Signal before changing lanes or exiting. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving left or right.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your physical condition does not make you drive unsafely?

options.text: Stay physically fit and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Drive only within your physical limits.

questions.explanation: Your physical condition affects your ability to drive safely. Know your limits and only drive if it is safe for you to do so.
